mechanisms.name: Primary cilia biogenesis and ciliary trafficking via BBSome, IFT, and transition zone machinery
mechanisms.summary: The largest coherent functional theme in P10 is cilia biogenesis and ciliary protein trafficking. Bbs9 encodes a core subunit of the BBSome complex, which mediates retrograde trafficking of GPCRs and other signaling receptors out of cilia via interaction with intraflagellar transport (IFT) complexes. Cc2d2a localizes to the ciliary transition zone and facilitates Rab8-dependent vesicle fusion at the ciliary base; mutations in CC2D2A cause Joubert and Meckel syndromes. Ift74 (together with Ift81) forms the principal module for IFT of tubulin into assembling cilia. Sdccag8 encodes a centrosomal/basal body protein whose C-terminal domain interacts with cilia length regulators Ick/Cilk1 and Mak; truncation causes polydactyly, cystic kidney, and retinal degeneration. Tbc1d32/Bromi acts at the ciliogenic basal body to regulate both Hedgehog transduction and early steps of ciliary bud formation. Cep164 is a distal appendage protein that organizes the platform for ciliary vesicle docking and IFT recruitment at the mother centriole. Nme7/NDK7 is a microtubule-binding nucleoside diphosphate kinase preferentially expressed in ciliated cells and identified as a cilia-associated gene candidate in zebrafish crispant screens. Wdpcp (a WD-repeat PCP effector) is essential for ciliogenesis in human epithelial cells. Cfap36 is a cilia- and flagella-associated protein (distinctive gene). Taken together, the majority of program and distinctive genes define a coherent cilia biogenesis and trafficking module.

mechanisms.name: Endothelial primary cilia as mechanosensors for blood flow in brain vasculature
mechanisms.summary: Primary cilia on endothelial cells function as critical mechanosensors that detect fluid shear stress from blood flow and transduce it into intracellular signals. Endothelial cells bearing cilia are significantly more responsive to fluid shear stress (as measured by KLF2 induction) than non-ciliated cells; chemical removal of cilia abolishes this response. Primary cilia are found on endothelial cells in regions of low or disturbed flow, including in the embryonic and developing brain vasculature. In the context of postnatal brain vascular development, the cilia biogenesis genes of P10 (Bbs9, Cc2d2a, Wdpcp, Ift74, Nme7, Sdccag8, Tbc1d32, Cep164, Cfap36) would be required for endothelial cells to assemble functional primary cilia and thereby sense hemodynamic forces during network remodeling. WDPCP specifically modulates cilia beating via the MAPK/ERK pathway, connecting ciliary function to a major endothelial stress-signaling cascade. Thus the program's cilia genes likely underlie a mechanotransduction competency in postnatal brain endothelial cells.

mechanisms.name: CNS angiogenesis and blood-brain barrier maintenance via Norrin/Wnt-Fzd4 signaling, GATA2, and Endoglin
mechanisms.summary: The perturbation regulators of P10 — Fzd4, Gata2, and Eng — are three well-characterized drivers of brain endothelial identity and blood-brain barrier (BBB) function. Fzd4 (Frizzled-4) is the receptor for Norrin in canonical Wnt signaling and is essential for CNS vascular development and barrier integrity in the retina and cerebellum; its loss causes BBB/BRB breakdown through cell-autonomous mechanisms. Endoglin (Eng) is a TGF-β co-receptor specifically expressed on vascular endothelial cells; mutations cause hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia and haploinsufficiency elevates brain AVM risk, implicating it in cerebrovascular angiogenesis. GATA2 is a master endothelial transcription factor that controls endothelium-specific gene expression programs and epigenetic chromatin organization; it is also a regulator of endothelial HIF signaling and glycolytic adaptation. Tet1, a distinctive program gene, regulates DNA methylation dynamics in brain microvascular endothelial cells (BMVECs) and modulates angiogenic gene expression, placing it in the same epigenetic regulatory layer. Together these genes define a regulatory program governing CNS endothelial identity, postnatal BBB maturation, and angiogenic competence during brain development.

mechanisms.name: Primary cilia biogenesis: basal body docking, transition zone integrity, intraflagellar transport, and BBSome assembly
mechanisms.summary: The largest coordinated functional theme in P10 is the construction and maintenance of primary cilia. Multiple program genes encode core ciliary components: CC2D2A (Cc2d2a) and SDCCAG8 (Sdccag8) anchor the ciliary transition zone/diffusion barrier; CEP164 (Cep164) forms distal centriolar appendages that dock vesicles and recruit TTBK2 to initiate ciliogenesis; IFT74 (Ift74) partners with IFT81 to transport tubulin along the axoneme; BBS9 (Bbs9) is a structural subunit of the octameric BBSome that traffics membrane receptors into the cilium; WDPCP (Wdpcp) promotes cilia beating and is required for ciliogenesis; NME7 (Nme7) is an established ciliome member whose deletion causes primary ciliary dyskinesia; and TBC1D32/BROMI (Tbc1d32) is required for ciliogenesis and Hedgehog signaling through cilia. Distinctive genes reinforce this theme: IFT74, CEP164, and SDCCAG8 are archetypally ciliary, and CFAP36 (Cfap36) is annotated as a cilia-and-flagella-associated protein.

mechanisms.name: Primary cilia mechanosensing and blood-brain barrier maturation in brain endothelial cells
mechanisms.summary: In the specific cell-type context of brain endothelial cells, primary cilia serve as mechanosensors for blood-flow shear stress and as signaling organelles critical for postnatal blood-brain barrier (BBB) development. Reviews of brain vascular biology explicitly identify endothelial cilia as an emerging component of BBB genesis. Endothelial primary cilia in areas of low shear stress sensitize cells to fluid flow, amplifying the KLF2 shear response. Loss of ciliary function in vascular endothelial cells disrupts flow sensing, while manipulating ciliary length (rapamycin) alters mechanosensory sensitivity. The cilia/centrosome genes in P10 (Bbs9, Cc2d2a, Cep164, Ift74, Wdpcp, Nme7, Sdccag8, Tbc1d32, Cfap36) are thus collectively interpretable as supplying the ciliary apparatus needed for flow sensing and paracrine signaling during postnatal brain vascular maturation.

mechanisms.name: Wnt/Norrin-FZD4 signaling and endothelial identity regulators governing BBB and CNS vascular barrier formation
mechanisms.summary: The perturbation regulators of P10 — FZD4, GATA2, and Endoglin (ENG) — define a distinct layer of transcriptional and receptor-mediated control over brain endothelial identity and BBB integrity. FZD4 is the obligate receptor for the Norrin/Wnt ligand in CNS vasculature; FZD4-deficient mice lose BBB function, and bioengineered FZD4-selective agonists restore BBB integrity after ischemic injury. GATA2 is a master endothelial transcription factor required for VEGF-driven sprouting angiogenesis and is de-repressed by injury to activate angiogenic programs. Endoglin (ENG) is an endothelial TGF-β co-receptor whose haploinsufficiency causes hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia with brain AVMs, and it modulates angiogenesis and vascular integrity through the ALK1/ALK5 axis. These three regulators collectively tune the transcriptional state of the brain endothelial cells in which the ciliary P10 gene program operates.

mechanisms.name: Sprouting angiogenesis and tip cell identity in postnatal CNS vasculature
mechanisms.summary: The program is anchored by canonical tip cell markers Angpt2 and Cxcr4, together with the Cdc42 effector Cdc42ep3 that operates downstream of the tip-cell regulator Nrp1 to drive filopodial formation. Single-cell transcriptomic studies of postnatal mouse brain endothelium directly identify these as tip-cell-enriched genes, and the regulator logic is consistent: Nrp1 KO decreases the program (required for tip cell identity), while Tek/Tie2 KO increases it (Ang1/Tie2 normally promotes vessel quiescence/stalk identity, so its loss shifts cells toward tip cell state). Gabarapl1 (distinctive) promotes EPC migration and angiogenesis. Hopx is enriched in intracranial arterial ECs, marking a protective, specialized brain-EC state.

mechanisms.name: TGF-β/Tgfbr1 signaling specifying CNS endothelial tip cell identity and vascular maturation
mechanisms.summary: Tgfbr1 and Tgfbr2 knockouts both strongly decrease this program (log2fc -0.86 and -0.77), indicating TGF-β receptor signaling is required to maintain it. A key mechanistic anchor is that CNS-specific 'diving' tip cells (D-tip cells) guiding deep vascular plexus formation have uniquely high TGF-β signaling, and endothelial-specific deletion of ALK5/Tgfbr1 prevents their identity acquisition and deep plexus formation. This CNS-context dependency (opposite to peripheral TGF-β effects on tip cells) explains P11's brain endothelial specificity. TGF-β/ALK5 additionally represses Angpt2 in brain pericytes, linking the Tgfbr1/2 regulators to the core Angpt2 program gene.

mechanisms.name: Endothelial ion channel mechanosensing and membrane calcium signaling
mechanisms.summary: Kcnj2 (Kir2.1, inward rectifier K+ channel) and Cacna1c (L-type Ca2+ channel) are expressed in brain capillary endothelial cells and mediate mechanosensory responses to blood flow. Kir2.1 in capillaries of electrically active tissues senses extracellular K+ to contribute to functional hyperemia, making this channel particularly relevant for neurovascular coupling in postnatal brain. The distinctive gene Jph1 (Junctophilin-1) bridges the plasma membrane to the sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticulum, creating Ca2+ microdomains at PM-SR junctions critical for ion channel regulation in vascular cells. Syt12 (Synaptotagmin-12, distinctive) and Rgs6 (regulator of G-protein signaling) further support membrane calcium trafficking and GPCR signal modulation in these cells.

mechanisms.name: Angiogenic tip cell identity and filopodial guidance in postnatal brain vessels
mechanisms.summary: Multiple program genes are co-enriched in endothelial tip cells leading sprouting capillaries during postnatal brain vascularization. Cxcr4 and Angpt2 are robustly identified as tip-cell-enriched transcripts by retinal and brain endothelial transcriptomics. Nrp1 (perturbation regulator, KO reduces program) acts cell-autonomously in brain tip cells, enabling CDC42 activation and filopodial protrusion—a function linked mechanistically to CDC42 effector proteins (Cdc42ep3). Notch-dependent suppression of Angpt2 in stalk cells further confirms that Angpt2 marks the tip cell state opposed to Notch-activated stalk identity.

mechanisms.name: Dll4-Notch-CXCR4 axis coupling sprouting to arteriovenous specification
mechanisms.summary: In postnatal mice, Dll4/Notch signaling couples endothelial tip cell sprouting to arterial fate acquisition by controlling CXCR4 expression; tip cells that activate Notch upregulate CXCR4 to migrate and connect to the developing arterial circulation. HOPX is specifically upregulated in intracranial (versus extracranial) arterial endothelial cells, consistent with an arterial-identity role in the brain. Nrp1 is positioned downstream of Notch as a pivot: Notch downregulates Nrp1, which shifts cells from tip to stalk via Alk1/Alk5 TGF-β signaling, thus linking the sprouting-to-arterial transition to TGF-β pathway balance.

mechanisms.name: TGF-β/Angiopoietin-2 signaling axis for postnatal brain vascular integrity and remodeling
mechanisms.summary: The perturbation regulators Tgfbr1 and Tgfbr2 (both with negative log2fc upon KO, reducing this program) maintain postnatal CNS vascular integrity: endothelial Tgfbr2 deletion in neonatal mice causes brain micro-hemorrhages and failure of the angiogenic front to invade deeper neural tissue. TGF-β signaling also represses Angpt2 (a program gene) in brain vessels; loss of TGF-β/Alk5 signaling in pericytes de-represses Angpt2, causing germinal matrix hemorrhage, suggesting program P11 marks a TGF-β-dependent remodeling state in which Angpt2 is tightly regulated. Nrp1 links the tip-stalk decision to TGF-β signaling by limiting Smad2/3 activation through Alk1/Alk5.

mechanisms.name: Rho/Ras GTPase cytoskeletal regulation of endothelial sprouting, tip cell behavior, and junctional integrity
mechanisms.summary: Multiple program genes encode Rho/Ras GTPase regulators that directly control endothelial cytoskeletal dynamics, angiogenic sprouting, and junction stability. Tiam1 (Rac1 GEF) mediates Ras-Tiam1-Rac1-Pak1 signaling required for endothelial migration and barrier integrity. ARHGAP18 (RhoC GAP) is an endogenous negative regulator of angiogenesis that limits tip cell formation, stabilizes endothelial junctions, regulates microtubule stability, and mediates flow-dependent EC alignment—all consistent with postnatal vascular remodeling. RasGRP3 activates Ras-ERK signaling in developing blood vessels and regulates endothelial migration. Itga4 (integrin α4) participates in endothelial directional sprouting and migration. Additional Rho/Arf GAPs (Srgap2, Arap2) and scaffold proteins (Sorbs1) expand this cytoskeletal module. VEGFR2/Kdr as a perturbation regulator links growth factor signaling to this Ras/Rho axis.

mechanisms.name: LMO2-ETS1 endothelial transcription factor network driving angiogenic remodeling and tip cell identity
mechanisms.summary: Lmo2 and Ets1 are master endothelial transcription factors that together orchestrate angiogenic remodeling in postnatal development. LMO2 forms a complex with TAL1 to regulate VEGFR2, DLL4, and angiopoietin-2 specifically in tip cells during sprouting angiogenesis; Lmo2-null endothelial cells fail to contribute to angiogenic remodeling after embryonic day 10. ETS1 transduces VEGF signaling to globally promote RNA polymerase II pause release and drive angiogenesis; ETS1 loss reduces expression of Kdr, Cldn5, and other angiogenic genes in endothelial cells. The perturbation regulators Notch1 and Kdr intersect with this network: Notch1 variants disrupt hierarchical arterial-capillary-venous organization in brain vessels, and Kdr (VEGFR2) is a direct transcriptional target of ETS1. Additional TFs Zfp608 and Arid5b, and the Ras-Notch transducer Rasgrp3, likely expand this transcriptional module.

mechanisms.name: Wnt/Norrin-Fzd4 and TGFβ/endoglin signaling for CNS vascular development and blood-brain barrier specification
mechanisms.summary: The perturbation regulators Fzd4, Eng, and Tgfbr1 define a signaling axis that controls CNS vascular development and BBB integrity in postnatal brain. Norrin/Fzd4 canonical Wnt signaling is essential for postnatal retinal and brain vascular development and BBB/BRB maintenance; Fzd4 KO brain ECs are selectively eliminated from the vascular network. Wnt7a and Norrin systems partially overlap in CNS BBB maintenance. TGFβ receptor ALK5 (Tgfbr1) controls brain endothelial morphogenesis and BBB integrity: pericyte ALK5 drives TIMP3 to regulate EC morphogenesis in the developing brain, and ALK5/TGFβ signaling controls BBB permeability in brain ECs. Endoglin (Eng), an endothelial TGFβ co-receptor, is required for proper endothelial migration and arteriovenous patterning—its loss causes HHT with brain AVMs. Within the program genes, Quaking (Qk) supports endothelial cell cycle progression and angiogenic sprouting. Hmcn1 and Adamts5/12 likely contribute ECM remodeling support for vascular maturation.

mechanisms.name: TGF-β/BMP-ALK signaling drives brain endothelial ECM production and BBB maturation
mechanisms.summary: Brain endothelial cells in this program express a TGF-β/Wnt/β-catenin-regulated ECM gene set (Adamtsl2, Htra3) that has been directly identified in forebrain endothelial cells during neurovascular maturation. Htra3 provides extracellular TGF-β/BMP antagonism (feedback), while Skil/SnoN modulates intracellular TGF-β signaling by facilitating ALK1-Smad1/5 activity and repressing ALK5-Smad2/3, balancing pro-angiogenic versus barrier-promoting outputs. Tram2 (distinctive gene) supports type I collagen/ECM secretion via the ER translocon. The positive requirement for Tgfbr1 and Tgfbr2 (their KO reduces the program) is consistent with TGF-β signaling being a driver of this brain endothelial ECM/BBB maturation state.

mechanisms.name: Notch1-Nrp1-Vezf1 axis controlling tip/stalk cell specification and brain endothelial identity
mechanisms.summary: Nrp1 (neuropilin-1) suppresses the stalk-cell phenotype by limiting TGF-β/BMP signaling through ALK1 and ALK5; Notch1 downregulates Nrp1 to relieve this inhibition and drive stalk-cell behavior. This Notch1-Nrp1-TGF-β/BMP crosstalk axis integrates all three non-TGFβR perturbation regulators and the Skil/SnoN program gene into a coherent stalk/tip cell specification mechanism. Vezf1, an endothelial-specific zinc finger transcription factor, is expressed in human brain microvascular endothelial cells and regulates BBB-related genes (GLUT1, CLDN5), maintaining endothelial transcriptional identity. Ccm2 is required to prevent BMP6/TGF-β-driven EndMT in brain endothelial cells, thereby maintaining vascular identity against a pathological mesenchymal transition.

mechanisms.name: Microsomal CYP-mediated oxidative metabolism: xenobiotic detoxification and fatty acid hydroxylation
mechanisms.summary: P450 oxidoreductase (Por) is the obligate electron donor for all microsomal cytochrome P450 enzymes. In this program, Por provides electrons to Cyp2d40 (xenobiotic oxidation) and to the fatty acid ω-hydroxylases Cyp4a12a and Cyp4a12b (mouse orthologs of human CYP4A11). CYP4A enzymes catalyze ω-oxidation of long-chain fatty acids and are regulated by PPARα; their upregulation in fatty liver disease generates reactive lipid intermediates and contributes to oxidative stress and NAFLD pathogenesis. The co-expression of Por with multiple CYP family members defines a coherent microsomal mixed-function oxidase system active in pericentral hepatocytes.

mechanisms.name: Hepatic lipid uptake, de novo lipogenesis, and triglyceride/lipoprotein flux (MASLD context)
mechanisms.summary: A dense cluster of program genes and perturbation regulators converges on the full hepatic lipid-metabolic axis: fatty acid import (Slc27a2/FATP2), triglyceride esterification and storage (Dgat2), VLDL assembly and secretion (Mttp/Ldlr), and transcriptional control of de novo lipogenesis via the SREBP pathway (Insig1, Scap) and carbohydrate-responsive ChREBP (Mlxipl). The perturbation regulators of this program—particularly Insig1, Scap, Dgat2, and Mlxipl—are core effectors of hepatic lipid homeostasis whose perturbation most strongly shifts program activity in both young and aged conditions. Retsat (retinol saturase) generates 13,14-dihydroretinoic acid, an endogenous RXR ligand that couples retinoid signaling to PPAR/RXR-regulated lipid gene networks. This theme is directly relevant to MASLD pathogenesis.

mechanisms.name: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation: ADP/ATP exchange and electron transport chain
mechanisms.summary: Two program/distinctive genes anchor a mitochondrial energy-transduction theme: Slc25a31 (ANT4), a mitochondrial inner membrane ADP/ATP antiporter that exports newly synthesized ATP in exchange for cytosolic ADP, and Cox6a1, a nuclear-encoded subunit of cytochrome c oxidase (Complex IV) that catalyzes the terminal step of the electron transport chain. Liver expresses tissue-specific COX subunit isoforms (including Cox6a1) that tune OXPHOS capacity to hepatic metabolic demands. Hepatocyte mitochondrial function is impaired in aging and MASLD, and reduced OXPHOS contributes to the lipid overload phenotype.

mechanisms.name: Mevalonate pathway and post-squalene cholesterol biosynthesis
mechanisms.summary: Nearly every program and distinctive gene encodes a sequential enzyme in the mevalonate-to-cholesterol pathway. Acat2 and Hmgcs1 generate HMG-CoA from acetyl-CoA; Mvk, Pmvk and Mvd (distinctive genes) phosphorylate mevalonate to isopentenyl-PP; Idi1 isomerizes it; Fdps and Fdft1 condense units to squalene; Lss cyclises squalene to lanosterol; then Cyp51 (14α-demethylase), Tm7sf2, Msmo1, Nsdhl, Hsd17b7, Sc5d and Dhcr7 complete the post-lanosterol Bloch/Kandutsch-Russell routes to cholesterol. Acss2 supplies the acetyl-CoA substrate via acetate. Together these genes constitute the complete de novo cholesterol biosynthesis program in mouse hepatocytes.

mechanisms.name: SCAP/INSIG1-SREBP2 sterol-sensing feedback control of the cholesterol synthesis gene program
mechanisms.summary: The perturbation regulators Scap and Insig1 are the canonical sterol-sensing machinery that controls SREBP2 processing and thereby transcribes the entire cholesterol biosynthesis gene program. SCAP escorts SREBP2 from ER to Golgi for proteolytic activation; knockout of Scap reduces hepatic cholesterol synthesis by ~80%, explaining its strong negative perturbation effect on P21. Insig1 retains the SCAP-SREBP2 complex in the ER when sterols are sufficient; knockout of Insig1 therefore hyper-activates SREBP2 and upregulates cholesterol synthesis genes, consistent with the positive log2FC observed in P21. Ldlr (positive perturbation FC) provides the complementary uptake limb: its loss forces compensatory upregulation of de novo synthesis via SREBP2. This SCAP-INSIG1-LDLR triad is the master feedback circuit gating the P21 program activity in both young and aged hepatocytes.

mechanisms.name: Coordinate hepatic lipid output: VLDL-triglyceride assembly coupled to de novo sterol synthesis
mechanisms.summary: The perturbation regulators Dgat2 and Mttp control the final step of VLDL assembly and secretion: Dgat2 synthesises diacylglycerol/triglycerides for VLDL core loading, and Mttp transfers lipids onto ApoB. Their negative perturbation log2FC on P21 indicates that blocking VLDL-TG export attenuates the upstream cholesterol biosynthesis program. Literature shows these two are co-regulated with cholesterol synthesis in hepatocytes: cholesterol loading induces both Dgat2 and Mttp to package lipids for export, while VLDL secretion creates demand for hepatic cholesterol synthesis. In the context of MASLD/aging, impaired VLDL export (reduced Mttp/Dgat2 activity) leads to hepatic lipid accumulation and downregulates coordinated biosynthesis, linking this regulator pair to the core P21 program.

mechanisms.name: De novo cholesterol/sterol biosynthesis via the mevalonate pathway
mechanisms.summary: Virtually every program gene and distinctive gene encodes a sequential enzyme of the mevalonate–to–cholesterol biosynthesis cascade in hepatocytes: Acss2 and Acat2 supply and handle acetyl-CoA/cholesteryl esters at the top; Hmgcs1 synthesises HMG-CoA; Idi1, Fdps, Mvk, Pmvk, and Mvd convert mevalonate to farnesyl pyrophosphate; Fdft1 (squalene synthase) and Lss (lanosterol synthase) initiate the sterol ring; and Cyp51, Tm7sf2, Msmo1, Nsdhl, Hsd17b7, Sc5d, and Dhcr7 complete the post-lanosterol route to cholesterol. This constitutes a near-complete transcriptional up-regulation of the entire pathway within hepatocytes.

mechanisms.name: SREBP2–Scap–Insig1 transcriptional control of the mevalonate pathway
mechanisms.summary: The perturbation regulators Scap (strong negative log2fc in both aged and young, meaning Scap KO activates this program) and Insig1 (positive log2fc, meaning Insig1 KO suppresses it) are the canonical ER-anchored toggle that controls SREBP2 processing and its nuclear entry to transcribe every enzyme gene in Mechanism 1. Ldlr (positive log2fc) is a canonical SREBP2 target for cholesterol uptake that collaborates with the biosynthetic programme. Collectively, the perturbation regulators identify Scap as the programme activator, Insig1 as the brake, and Ldlr as the downstream uptake arm of the same transcriptional circuit.

mechanisms.name: Dysregulation of hepatic cholesterol synthesis in MASLD and liver aging
mechanisms.summary: The mevalonate/cholesterol biosynthesis pathway is elevated in fatty liver (MASLD) and contributes to hepatic senescence during aging. SREBP1/2-driven sterol synthesis promotes steatosis, and mevalonate pathway activity directly induces cellular senescence via ERRα and mitochondrial dysfunction in liver. The perturbation regulators Dgat2 and Mttp — whose knockdown is the strongest activator of this program — connect triglyceride synthesis and VLDL-coupled cholesterol esterification (Acat2) to the sterol programme, suggesting that impaired VLDL export liberates free cholesterol and amplifies mevalonate pathway transcription.

mechanisms.name: Carbohydrate-responsive hepatic de novo lipogenesis
mechanisms.summary: Multiple program genes encode enzymes that convert glucose and fructose carbons into lipogenic building blocks: Khk phosphorylates fructose to fructose-1-phosphate, Pklr drives pyruvate production from glycolysis, Acly cleaves citrate to generate cytosolic acetyl-CoA, and Me1 supplies NADPH for reductive fatty acid synthesis. The master perturbation regulator Mlxipl (ChREBP) transcriptionally activates this entire DNL gene set in response to intracellular sugar signals, while Gckr regulates hepatic glucokinase activity and glucose flux into the pathway. This coordinated program is strongly implicated in MASLD pathogenesis through excess hepatic triglyceride accumulation.

mechanisms.name: Hepatic xenobiotic detoxification and reactive aldehyde/ROS defense
mechanisms.summary: A second coherent cluster consists of enzymes that defend hepatocytes against cytotoxic aldehydes, electrophiles, and ROS. Aldh2 oxidizes acetaldehyde and lipid-derived aldehydes (4-HNE) in mitochondria. Gstm7, Gstp1, and Gstp3 conjugate glutathione to electrophilic xenobiotics and lipid peroxidation products. Ugdh generates UDP-glucuronate for glucuronidation-based clearance. Cyb5r3 mediates NADH-dependent reduction at the outer mitochondrial membrane. Mt1 and Mt2 are inducible metal-binding proteins that scavenge ROS and heavy metals. Lias synthesizes lipoic acid, an essential mitochondrial antioxidant cofactor. This detoxification suite is relevant to hepatocyte resilience under the oxidative conditions of MASLD and aging.

mechanisms.name: Lipid/sterol sensing and triglyceride synthesis regulation
mechanisms.summary: A third cluster, dominated by perturbation regulators, controls the downstream storage of newly synthesized lipids and sterol homeostasis. Insig1 retains SREBP precursors in the ER under high-sterol conditions, gating VLDL secretion and hepatic cholesterol accumulation in MASH. Dgat2 catalyzes the final committed step of triglyceride synthesis and modulates SREBP-1 cleavage via ER phospholipid composition. Scap is the sterol-sensing escort for SREBP processing. Together these regulators couple the acetyl-CoA produced by Acly to downstream sterol and TG synthesis, coordinating lipid output with cellular sterol status—a balance disrupted in both MASLD and aging.

mechanisms.name: Pericentral (zone 3) xenobiotic and drug metabolism
mechanisms.summary: Cyp2e1 and Cyp4b1 are cytochrome P450 enzymes that define pericentral (zone 3) hepatocytes and catalyze phase I oxidative metabolism of xenobiotics, drugs, and ethanol. Mgst1 provides complementary phase II glutathione conjugation of electrophilic metabolites, protecting against oxidative damage. Ces1d (carboxylesterase 1d) hydrolyzes ester-bond-containing xenobiotics and drugs. This pericentral xenobiotic gene cluster is under Wnt/β-catenin signaling control that establishes zone 3 identity. In aging and MASLD, disruption of this pericentral metabolic niche underlies heightened hepatotoxicity susceptibility.

mechanisms.name: Peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation and lipid droplet dynamics
mechanisms.summary: Acox1 (acyl-CoA oxidase 1) catalyzes the rate-limiting step of peroxisomal β-oxidation and is a key PPARα target; its loss accelerates NAFLD progression. Fitm1 (FIT1) is an ER-resident protein essential for lipid droplet biogenesis in liver. Ces1d hydrolyzes stored triglycerides in hepatocytes, linking lipid droplet turnover to oxidation. Pon1 is synthesized in the liver and associated with HDL-mediated reverse cholesterol transport; its activity is suppressed in hepatic steatosis. Chpt1 synthesizes phosphatidylcholine, critical for VLDL assembly and lipid export. Together these genes control hepatic lipid partitioning between storage, oxidation, and export—a balance disrupted in MASLD and aging.

mechanisms.name: SREBP-driven lipogenesis and sterol biosynthesis suppressed by hepatokines Mup10/17
mechanisms.summary: Perturbation regulators Srebf1 (SREBP1c), Scap, and Sqle form a lipogenic/cholesterogenic axis in hepatocytes: SCAP escorts SREBP1 to Golgi for cleavage, activating lipogenic genes including SQLE (rate-limiting cholesterol synthesis enzyme) and Dgat2. This axis is amplified in MASLD and aged liver. Mup10 and Mup17 are liver-derived hepatokines that suppress this lipogenic program—MUP1 inhibits gluconeogenic and lipogenic gene expression in hepatocytes, and MUP levels fall markedly in NAFLD/ER stress, removing a brake on lipogenesis. Pparg amplifies lipid uptake. This mechanism frames the program as a hepatocyte-intrinsic lipogenic regulatory module whose balance is eroded in aging and MASLD.

mechanisms.name: Periportal amino acid catabolism and urea cycle nitrogen disposal
mechanisms.summary: Multiple genes in this program converge on periportal hepatocyte catabolism of amino acids and disposal of resulting nitrogen via the urea cycle. Hal and Uroc1 catabolize histidine; Sds converts serine to pyruvate; Gls2 hydrolyzes glutamine releasing ammonia; Uox degrades purines; Cps1 is the rate-limiting urea cycle enzyme that fixes NH3 into carbamoyl phosphate; Sfxn1 transports serine into mitochondria supporting one-carbon flux linked to nitrogen handling; Rida processes reactive deaminated intermediates. These enzymes are classically co-expressed in the periportal zone and are downregulated together in NAFLD/MASLD and modulated by aging-related O-GlcNAcylation.

mechanisms.name: Hepatic gluconeogenesis and periportal glucose output regulated by insulin signaling
mechanisms.summary: Pck1 (PEPCK1) is the rate-limiting gluconeogenic enzyme in periportal hepatocytes; Sds feeds pyruvate as gluconeogenic substrate; Gls2-derived α-ketoglutarate also enters gluconeogenesis. The insulin receptor (Insr) and its substrate Irs1 suppress Pck1 transcription postprandially; insulin resistance in aging and MASLD causes excess hepatic glucose production. Pck1 also phosphorylates INSIG1/2 (a young-condition perturbation regulator) at the ER, linking gluconeogenesis to SREBP-mediated lipogenesis and potentially contributing to MASLD steatosis.

mechanisms.name: Hepatocyte steroid, bile acid, and xenobiotic sulfation/hydroxysteroid metabolism
mechanisms.summary: Sult2a2 (hydroxysteroid sulfotransferase) sulfonates bile acids, hydroxysteroids, and procarcinogen xenobiotics in hepatocytes and is regulated by PPARα, a key lipid-sensing nuclear receptor activated in MASLD. Hsd17b6 is a 3α-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase expressed almost exclusively in hepatocytes that catalyzes androgen synthesis and is correlated with fatty liver disease, though its direct causal role in MASLD is dispensable in isolation. Slco1b2 (a perturbation regulator) encodes the hepatic organic anion transporter OATP1B2 that mediates uptake of bile acids and other conjugated substrates channeled to sulfation. Together, these genes represent hepatocyte-specific steroid/bile acid/xenobiotic processing capacity that is perturbed in MASLD.

mechanisms.name: Hepatic Phase I/II xenobiotic detoxification and steroid/bile acid conjugation
mechanisms.summary: The program encodes a comprehensive hepatic detoxification apparatus spanning Phase I oxidoreduction (Cyp2c50, Akr1c6, Aldh1a1, Aldh3a2) and Phase II conjugation (Gsta3, Sult2a5, Sult2a7, Sult2a8). The three SULT2A paralogs catalyze bile acid and steroid sulfation to enhance their solubility and biliary/urinary elimination. Aldh1a1 and Aldh3a2 oxidize reactive aldehydes arising from lipid peroxidation and xenobiotic metabolism. Gsta3 combines glutathione conjugation with steroid isomerase activity. This ensemble is characteristic of pericentral hepatocytes that execute high-throughput chemical detoxification and is altered both in hepatic aging and in MASLD/NASH. Perturbation regulators Tpst1 (sulfation of tyrosine residues) and Insig1 (sterol sensing, regulates bile acid feedback) are functionally aligned with this theme.

mechanisms.name: Lipid droplet biogenesis and peroxisomal/ER fatty acid catabolism
mechanisms.summary: A second coherent theme involves the formation of lipid droplets and the peroxisomal/ER catabolism of fatty acids. Fitm1 (FITM1) is an ER-resident transmembrane protein that directly binds triglyceride to partition it into lipid droplets. Hao2 is a peroxisomal hydroxy-acid oxidase involved in glyoxylate and short/medium-chain hydroxy-fatty acid oxidation. Eci2 encodes a peroxisomal enoyl-CoA delta isomerase required for beta-oxidation of unsaturated fatty acids. Cyb5b is an ER cytochrome b5 that donates electrons for fatty acid desaturation. Aldh3a2 (fatty aldehyde dehydrogenase) converts toxic fatty aldehydes generated during peroxisomal/microsomal lipid oxidation. Lonp2 is the peroxisomal Lon protease responsible for degrading oxidized or misfolded peroxisomal matrix proteins. The aggregate function is hepatic lipid homeostasis—coordinating lipid droplet loading, peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation and ER fatty acid remodeling—processes that are directly dysregulated in MASLD. Regulators Dgat2 (triglyceride synthesis) and Abcg5 (biliary sterol secretion) define the boundaries of this lipid flux.

mechanisms.name: Sulfur amino acid catabolism and nitrogen/ammonia detoxification (urea cycle support)
mechanisms.summary: A third mechanism centers on hepatic sulfur amino acid catabolism and nitrogen disposal. Cdo1 (cysteine dioxygenase 1) is the gate-keeping enzyme that irreversibly oxidizes cysteine to cysteine sulfinic acid, committing it to taurine synthesis (for bile acid conjugation) or to sulfate/pyruvate. Cdo1 expression is regulated by bile acid/FXR signaling and its hepatocyte-specific deletion increases GSH capacity and protection from oxidative stress. Car5a (carbonic anhydrase VA, highly liver-enriched) supplies bicarbonate to carbamoylphosphate synthetase 1, the rate-limiting urea cycle enzyme for ammonia detoxification; Car5a knockout mice show impaired ureagenesis. Agmat (agmatinase) catabolizes agmatine to putrescine + urea, feeding into polyamine synthesis from arginine. Together these genes support the hepatic capacity to safely dispose of nitrogen and sulfur from amino acid catabolism. Aging regulator G6pc (glucose-6-phosphatase) is co-expressed in this periportal metabolic zone, and Insr regulates urea cycle enzyme activities via insulin signaling.

mechanisms.name: Phase I/II xenobiotic, steroid, and bile acid detoxification (Nrf2/CAR-regulated hepatocyte program)
mechanisms.summary: Multiple program genes encode consecutive enzymatic steps that oxidise, reduce, and conjugate endogenous steroids, bile acids, and xenobiotics. Sult2a5, Sult2a7, and Sult2a8 are bile acid/steroid sulfotransferases that sulfate hydroxy-bile acids and DHEA-like steroids to render them excretable. Gsta3 conjugates electrophilic substrates to glutathione (phase II), Akr1c6 performs ketone/aldehyde reductions (phase I), Aldh1a1 oxidises reactive aldehydes, and Cyp2c50 is a cytochrome P450 oxidase—all induced together by the Nrf2 transcription factor in mouse liver. Cyb5b supplies electrons to CYP450s and the outer-mitochondrial amidoxime reductase system for xenobiotic detoxification. The CAR nuclear receptor coordinately up-regulates Sult2a1-type enzymes together with the Mrp4 bile acid sulfate exporter as a cholestasis-protective mechanism. Perturbation regulator Abcg5 (ABC transporter for biliary cholesterol/sterol excretion) is likewise a direct Nrf2 target, connecting sterol detoxification flux to excretion.

mechanisms.name: Peroxisomal and microsomal fatty acid catabolism and lipid aldehyde detoxification
mechanisms.summary: A second cluster of program genes collectively executes peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation and clears toxic lipid-derived aldehydes. Hao2 (HAOX2) is a peroxisomal 2-hydroxy acid oxidase expressed predominantly in liver that oxidises 2-hydroxy fatty acids as part of the alpha-oxidation pathway. Eci2 is the enoyl-CoA isomerase required to handle double bonds at odd-numbered positions during beta-oxidation of unsaturated fatty acids, with both mitochondrial and peroxisomal isoforms in liver. Aldh3a2 (FALDH, fatty aldehyde dehydrogenase) converts long-chain fatty aldehydes released during peroxisomal alpha-oxidation or lipid peroxidation to fatty acids; it is expressed in liver microsomes, regulated by insulin, and protects against lipid-derived oxidative stress. Fitm1 is an ER-resident transmembrane protein that directly binds triglyceride and partitions it into lipid droplets. Lonp2 (a peroxisomal Lon-type protease) maintains quality control of peroxisomal enzymes. Perturbation regulators Dgat2 (triglyceride synthesis) and Flcn (mTORC1/peroxisome biogenesis) modulate flux through this oxidative axis.

mechanisms.name: Hepatic cysteine catabolism, taurine biosynthesis, and sulfur amino acid homeostasis
mechanisms.summary: Cdo1, a program gene and among the most hepatocyte-enriched enzymes, is the rate-limiting enzyme converting cysteine to cysteine sulfinic acid—the entry point for taurine synthesis and a major determinant of hepatic cysteine availability, GSH production, and cholesterol handling. Bile acid/FXR signalling represses CDO1, tightly coupling sulfur amino acid flux to the bile acid cycle. CDO1 activity also controls gluconeogenesis by limiting hepatic cysteine (knockdown of CDO1 raises liver cysteine and glucose output; PMID 39819116), linking it to perturbation regulator G6pc (glucose-6-phosphatase). Agmat (agmatinase, a distinctive gene) catalyses agmatine hydrolysis in the urea/polyamine pathway, and Car5a (mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase V) supplies HCO3⁻ for carbamoyl phosphate synthetase in ureagenesis—both extending the nitrogen/amine detoxification axis. Rgn/SMP30, a program gene, is a calcium-binding protein that declines progressively with aging in hepatocytes, directly matching the aging condition of this program. Sord (sorbitol dehydrogenase) participates in polyol/fructose metabolism in liver and is co-regulated with NRF2 target genes under metabolic stress. Perturbation regulators Insr and G6pc converge on the glucose–amino acid homeostasis nexus that CDO1 participates in.

assessor_text.text: Nucleoside diphosphate (NDP) kinase is an enzyme that synthesizes the nucleoside triphosphates. In mammals, nine sequences (NDK1-NDK9) have been found with domain(s) homologous to the catalytic domain of NDP kinase, and some of them have been shown to associate with sperm flagella. The present study examines the localization of NDK7, for which little information has been available. Database analysis showed that the NDK7 gene is present in organisms with cilia and flagella. Western blotting analyses of various mouse tissues consistently indicated that NDK7 is preferentially expressed in tissues with motile cilia as well as in sperm. Immunofluorescence microscopy revealed that this protein is localized along the entire length of the TritonX-100-insoluble fraction of sperm flagella, possibly in the axonemes. Unexpectedly, however, NDK7 in tracheal epithelia was found in the cell body but not in cilia. Finally, in vitro co-sedimentation assays using recombinant proteins showed that both mouse and Chlamydomonas NDK7 directly bind to microtubules.

review_items.mechanism_name: Primary cilia biogenesis and ciliary trafficking via BBSome, IFT, and transition zone machinery
review_items.mechanism_summary: The largest coherent functional theme in P10 is cilia biogenesis and ciliary protein trafficking. Bbs9 encodes a core subunit of the BBSome complex, which mediates retrograde trafficking of GPCRs and other signaling receptors out of cilia via interaction with intraflagellar transport (IFT) complexes. Cc2d2a localizes to the ciliary transition zone and facilitates Rab8-dependent vesicle fusion at the ciliary base; mutations in CC2D2A cause Joubert and Meckel syndromes. Ift74 (together with Ift81) forms the principal module for IFT of tubulin into assembling cilia. Sdccag8 encodes a centrosomal/basal body protein whose C-terminal domain interacts with cilia length regulators Ick/Cilk1 and Mak; truncation causes polydactyly, cystic kidney, and retinal degeneration. Tbc1d32/Bromi acts at the ciliogenic basal body to regulate both Hedgehog transduction and early steps of ciliary bud formation. Cep164 is a distal appendage protein that organizes the platform for ciliary vesicle docking and IFT recruitment at the mother centriole. Nme7/NDK7 is a microtubule-binding nucleoside diphosphate kinase preferentially expressed in ciliated cells and identified as a cilia-associated gene candidate in zebrafish crispant screens. Wdpcp (a WD-repeat PCP effector) is essential for ciliogenesis in human epithelial cells. Cfap36 is a cilia- and flagella-associated protein (distinctive gene). Taken together, the majority of program and distinctive genes define a coherent cilia biogenesis and trafficking module.

paper.title: NDP kinase 7 is a conserved microtubule-binding protein preferentially expressed in ciliated cells.

review_items.selection_reason: Nme7/NDK7 is a conserved microtubule-binding protein preferentially expressed in ciliated mammalian tissues.

assessor_text.text: The cardiovascular system is exposed to biochemical and biomechanical signals. Various sensors for these signals have been described and they contribute to cardiovascular development, maintenance of vessel integrity during adult life, and to pathogenesis. In the past 10years, primary cilia, membrane-covered, rod-like cellular protrusions, were discovered on multiple cell types of the cardiovascular system. Primary cilia are sensory organelles involved in several key (developmental) signaling pathways and in chemo- and mechanosensing on a myriad of cell types. In the embryonic and adult cardiovascular system, they have been demonstrated to function as shear stress sensors on endothelial cells and could act as strain sensors on smooth muscle cells and cardiomyocytes and as chemosensors on fibroblasts. This review will cover their occurrence and elaborate on established and possible functions of primary cilia in the cardiovascular system.

review_items.mechanism_name: Endothelial primary cilia as mechanosensors for blood flow in brain vasculature
review_items.mechanism_summary: Primary cilia on endothelial cells function as critical mechanosensors that detect fluid shear stress from blood flow and transduce it into intracellular signals. Endothelial cells bearing cilia are significantly more responsive to fluid shear stress (as measured by KLF2 induction) than non-ciliated cells; chemical removal of cilia abolishes this response. Primary cilia are found on endothelial cells in regions of low or disturbed flow, including in the embryonic and developing brain vasculature. In the context of postnatal brain vascular development, the cilia biogenesis genes of P10 (Bbs9, Cc2d2a, Wdpcp, Ift74, Nme7, Sdccag8, Tbc1d32, Cep164, Cfap36) would be required for endothelial cells to assemble functional primary cilia and thereby sense hemodynamic forces during network remodeling. WDPCP specifically modulates cilia beating via the MAPK/ERK pathway, connecting ciliary function to a major endothelial stress-signaling cascade. Thus the program's cilia genes likely underlie a mechanotransduction competency in postnatal brain endothelial cells.

paper.title: Role for primary cilia as flow detectors in the cardiovascular system.

review_items.selection_reason: Comprehensive review: endothelial primary cilia act as shear stress sensors in developing and adult cardiovascular system.

assessor_text.text: GATA2 is well recognized as a key transcription factor and regulator of cell-type specificity and differentiation. Here, we carried out comparative chromatin immunoprecipitation with comprehensive sequencing (ChIP-seq) to determine genome-wide occupancy of GATA2 in endothelial cells and erythroids, and compared the occupancy to the respective gene expression profile in each cell type. Although GATA2 was commonly expressed in both cell types, different GATA2 bindings and distinct cell-specific gene expressions were observed. By using the ChIP-seq with epigenetic histone modifications and chromatin conformation capture assays; we elucidated the mechanistic regulation of endothelial-specific GATA2-mediated endomucin gene expression, that was regulated by the endothelial-specific chromatin loop with a GATA2-associated distal enhancer and core promoter. Knockdown of endomucin markedly attenuated endothelial cell growth, migration and tube formation. Moreover, abrogation of GATA2 in endothelium demonstrated not only a reduction of endothelial-specific markers, but also induction of mesenchymal transition promoting gene expression. Our findings provide new insights into the correlation of endothelial-expressed GATA2 binding, epigenetic modification, and the determination of endothelial cell specificity.

review_items.mechanism_name: CNS angiogenesis and blood-brain barrier maintenance via Norrin/Wnt-Fzd4 signaling, GATA2, and Endoglin
review_items.mechanism_summary: The perturbation regulators of P10 — Fzd4, Gata2, and Eng — are three well-characterized drivers of brain endothelial identity and blood-brain barrier (BBB) function. Fzd4 (Frizzled-4) is the receptor for Norrin in canonical Wnt signaling and is essential for CNS vascular development and barrier integrity in the retina and cerebellum; its loss causes BBB/BRB breakdown through cell-autonomous mechanisms. Endoglin (Eng) is a TGF-β co-receptor specifically expressed on vascular endothelial cells; mutations cause hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia and haploinsufficiency elevates brain AVM risk, implicating it in cerebrovascular angiogenesis. GATA2 is a master endothelial transcription factor that controls endothelium-specific gene expression programs and epigenetic chromatin organization; it is also a regulator of endothelial HIF signaling and glycolytic adaptation. Tet1, a distinctive program gene, regulates DNA methylation dynamics in brain microvascular endothelial cells (BMVECs) and modulates angiogenic gene expression, placing it in the same epigenetic regulatory layer. Together these genes define a regulatory program governing CNS endothelial identity, postnatal BBB maturation, and angiogenic competence during brain development.

paper.title: Epigenetically coordinated GATA2 binding is necessary for endothelium-specific endomucin expression.

review_items.selection_reason: GATA2 ChIP-seq shows endothelium-specific binding coordinating endothelial identity genes; GATA2 loss induces endothelial-mesenchymal transition.

assessor_text.text: The primary cilium is a microtubule-based organelle required for Hedgehog (Hh) signaling and consists of a basal body, a ciliary axoneme and a compartment between the first two structures, called the transition zone (TZ). The TZ serves as a gatekeeper to control protein composition in cilia, but less is known about its role in ciliary bud formation. Here, we show that centrosomal protein Dzip1l is required for Hh signaling between Smoothened and Sufu. Dzip1l colocalizes with basal body appendage proteins and Rpgrip1l, a TZ protein. Loss of Dzip1l results in reduced ciliogenesis and dysmorphic cilia in vivo Dzip1l interacts with, and acts upstream of, Cby, an appendage protein, in ciliogenesis. Dzip1l also has overlapping functions with Bromi (Tbc1d32) in ciliogenesis, cilia morphogenesis and neural tube patterning. Loss of Dzip1l arrests ciliogenesis at the stage of ciliary bud formation from the TZ. Consistent with this, Dzip1l mutant cells fail to remove the capping protein Cp110 (Ccp110) from the distal end of mother centrioles and to recruit Rpgrip1l to the TZ. Therefore, Dzip1l promotes ciliary bud formation and is required for the integrity of the TZ.

assessor_text.text:
Ciliopathies are a recently defined and rapidly growing group of human disorders caused by dysfunction of primary cilia which are microtubule-based organelles present on the surface of most differentiated cell types (1–3). Despite significant functional differences in diverse cell types, all primary cilia share a common basic structure consisting of a circular array of nine microtubule doublets forming the axoneme, which is anchored in the basal body, a modified centriole (4–6). Dysfunction of primary cilia results in a spectrum of phenotypes including central nervous system malformations, retinal dystrophy and cystic kidney disease as illustrated in Bardet–Biedl syndrome (MIM 209900), Joubert syndrome (MIM 213300) or Senior-Løken syndrome (MIM 266900), among others (7). Zebrafish models for ciliopathies [sco/arl13b, ift88 and ift57 mutants (8–11); cep290, bbs and nphp gene morphants (12–16)] recapitulate the cystic kidney and retinal phenotypes and offer insight into the mechanisms underlying these defects (17,18).

The photoreceptor outer segment is a specialized primary cilium consisting of a microtubule-based axoneme and regular stacks of membrane folds or disks containing the photopigments (opsins) required for the phototransduction cascade (17,19). Development/maintenance of the outer segment requires transport of at least some of its components by complex networks of proteins involved in: (i) vesicle sorting and trafficking from the Golgi to the base of the cilium, (ii) docking at the base of the cilium and fusion with the periciliary membrane and (iii) transport within the ciliary shaft dependent on intra-flagellar transport (IFT) (19,20). The vesicle trafficking steps are controlled by several small GTPases from the Rab family among which Rab8 plays a central role in fusion of opsin-carrier vesicles at the base of the cilium (21). Roles for Rab8 in photoreceptor outer segment disk morphogenesis (22) and ciliary membrane biogenesis in cooperation with the BBSome (23) have also been shown.

Joubert syndrome (MIM 213300) is an autosomal recessive human ciliopathy characterized by cerebellar vermis hypoplasia associated with variable involvement of other organ systems, including retinal dystrophy and cystic kidney disease (24–27). Significant genetic heterogeneity underlies Joubert syndrome with 11 causative genes identified to date: CC2D2A, RPGRIP1L, NPHP1, AHI1, CEP290, TMEM67 (MKS3), ARL13B, INPP5E, OFD1, TMEM216 and TCTN2 (12,28–38). Their products localize to the basal body, transition zone (39–42) and/or ciliary axoneme (31,32) and are involved in a number of ciliary-related functions, including ciliogenesis [ARL13b (11), TMEM216 (40), AHI1 (42) or CEP290 (43)] and regulation of ciliary protein content [ARL13B (44), RPGRIP1L (41), AHI1 (45), CEP290 (39), MKS3 (41)]. In addition, a role in vesicle trafficking has been suggested for AHI1 and CEP290 based on their interaction with Rab8 (42,43). Mice deficient for these genes display abnormal retinal photoreceptor outer segments and opsin mislocalization (45–47).

The Joubert-associated protein CC2D2A localizes to the base of the cilium in cultured retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and kidney (IMCD3) cells (30), and contains a phospholipid-binding C2 domain found in proteins involved in vesicle fusion and trafficking (48), as well as coiled-coil domains found in many ciliary proteins. Tallila et al. (49) reported absence of cilia in cultured human fibroblasts homozygous for a CC2D2A mutation and therefore proposed that CC2D2A is required for cilium formation. More recent work using Caenorhabditis elegans localized CC2D2A protein to the transition zone of amphid and phasmid neuron cilia and found no structural cilium defects in cc2d2a-mutant worms (41). This study proposed that CC2D2A functions in a complex with other ciliopathy-associated proteins at the transition zone of cilia as a ‘gate-keeper’, restricting proteins from inappropriately entering the cilium. This function is similar to what has been described for CEP290 in a Chlamydomonas model (39).

We previously reported a zebrafish cc2d2a mutant (snl/cc2d2aw38), harboring a nonsense mutation up-stream of the C2 domain (W628X), that displays a cystic kidney phenotype (30,50). This phenotype was enhanced by partial knock-down of cep290, indicating a genetic interaction between cc2d2a and cep290. Furthermore, a physical interaction between the products of these genes was demonstrated (30). In this new work, we explore the cell-biological role of Cc2d2a in zebrafish photoreceptors. We show that Cc2d2a localizes to the connecting cilium/transition zone of cilia in photoreceptors and various other cells and is required for outer segment development and normal visual function. Our analysis reveals mislocalization of transmembrane outer segment proteins (opsins) and striking accumulation of vesicles in mutant photoreceptors, suggesting a role for Cc2d2a in vesicle trafficking and fusion. This is further supported by mislocalization of Rab8 in cc2d2a−/− photoreceptors and by a synergistic effect between cc2d2a and rab8 in vivo. We also demonstrate that cilia are present in photoreceptors and other cell types where cc2d2a is normally expressed, arguing against a primary function for Cc2d2a in ciliogenesis. Our data support a model where Cc2d2a, localized at the connecting cilium of the photoreceptor, functions in Rab8-dependent trafficking and fusion of opsin-carrier vesicles.

Previous phenotypic analysis of the cc2d2aw38 zebrafish mutant (hereafter referred to as cc2d2a mutant or cc2d2a−/−) revealed a sinusoidal body shape in larvae and adults (50) (Supplementary Material, Fig. S1A and B) and an incompletely penetrant pronephric (kidney) cyst phenotype with 30–50% of homozygous mutants developing cysts by 3 days post-fertilization (d.p.f.) (30). Given the retinal dystrophy seen in human patients with CC2D2A-associated Joubert syndrome (30,51), we evaluated the eyes of homozygous cc2d2a zebrafish mutants (cc2d2a+/− embryos were indistinguishable from wild-type embryos in all assays). While overall eye size and retinal lamination are unaffected on light microscopy (Fig. 1A and B and Supplementary Material, Fig. S1C and D), rod and cone outer segments are short and disorganized in cc2d2a−/− fish compared with wild-type and heterozygous siblings at 5 d.p.f. (red brackets in Fig. 1A–D). This phenotype is variable even within a single-mutant retina, ranging from shortened but otherwise normally shaped outer segments to complete absence of outer segments. Intermediate severity is most commonly observed, with disorganized whorls of membrane visible above the mitochondria in the inner segment of the photoreceptors (red arrow in Fig. 1D and F). Apical–basal polarity is unaffected based on preservation of the characteristic photoreceptor cell body shape, highlighted with the zpr1 antibody which marks red/green cones (52) (Fig. 1J′), as well as the normal distribution of organelles as viewed by transmission electron microscopy (Fig. 1D). To determine whether outer segments initially form normally and subsequently degenerate in cc2d2a mutants, we used the tg(TaCP:MCFP) line, in which membrane-tagged CFP is expressed under the transducin promoter specifically in cone photoreceptors, thereby highlighting all cone outer segments (53). MCFP expression is robustly detected at 80 h post-fertilization (h.p.f.) in cryosections from wild-type embryos demonstrating well-organized nascent cone outer segments (Fig. 1G). In cc2d2a−/− retinas, few outer segments are visible, and these appear short and disorganized even at this early stage, indicating that outer segment formation is never achieved normally (Fig. 1H). Other zebrafish mutants with abnormal or absent photoreceptor outer segments such as ift88, ift57, fleer and elipsa all display significant photoreceptor cell loss, predominantly in the central retina, by 5d.p.f. (8,54). In contrast, cc2d2a−/− embryos have relatively normal numbers of photoreceptors at this stage as shown by immunostaining of cryosections with zpr1, which marks red–green cones (52) (Fig. 1I and J), and 4c12, which marks rods (55) (Supplementary Material, Fig. S1G and H). In addition, we did not observe increased cell death based on caspase staining at 4 d.p.f. (Supplementary Material, Fig. S1F). In contrast, retinas from 4-week-old cc2d2a−/− fish show moderate loss of photoreceptors, as shown by zpr1 (Fig. 1K and L) and 4c12 (Supplementary Material, Fig. S1I and J) staining. This loss of photoreceptors is even more clearly visible using bodipy counterstaining (Supplementary Material, Fig. S1K and L) which highlights cell membranes and membrane-rich outer segments, thereby indicating that photoreceptor cell loss does occur in cc2d2a mutants, but at a slower rate than in other ciliopathy mutants. Based on these data, we conclude that Cc2d2a is required for photoreceptor outer segment development and maintenance, and that its deficiency leads to slow photoreceptor degeneration.

Given the retinal photoreceptor phenotype observed in homozygous cc2d2a mutants, we evaluated the mutant fish for abnormal visual function. A small proportion of homozygous cc2d2a mutants are viable to adulthood, and although small and morphologically highly abnormal (Supplementary Material, Fig. S1A and B), they display some visual function based on relatively normal feeding behavior and responsiveness to objects moving in front of the tank. We performed optokinetic response testing (56,57) in 5d.p.f. larvae and found no obvious difference in unquantified eye movements between mutants and their wild-type or heterozygote siblings at high-contrast conditions (data not shown). However, electroretinogram (ERG) recordings (58) at 5 and 6d.p.f., using a series of light intensities, revealed significantly decreased responses in mutants compared with wild-type and heterozygous siblings at all tested conditions (Fig. 2). Therefore, the observed retinal photoreceptor outer segment phenotype is associated with decreased visual sensitivity in cc2d2a mutant zebrafish. The products of Joubert/ciliopathy spectrum genes localize to specific segments of the cilium, ranging from the basal body [AHI1 (42), for example] to the ciliary axoneme [ARL13B (32) or INPP5E (31)], and their precise localization can be informative with respect to their function in ciliary biology. We previously showed that CC2D2A co-localizes at the base of cilia with CEP290 in cultured RPE cells (30). In addition, a recent work has shown that the C. elegans CC2D2A ortholog, along with a subset of other ciliopathy proteins, localizes to the transition zone (41), a region at the base of the cilium just apical to the basal body. To determine whether this subcellular localization is conserved in photoreceptors and other ciliated cell types, we developed a monoclonal antibody against amino acids 430–1019 of the zebrafish protein. This antibody detects a protein of the expected 191 kDa molecular weight in lysates from 48 h.p.f. wild-type embryos but not in lysates from embryos lacking Cc2d2a (Fig. 3I), indicating lack of full-length Cc2d2a protein in cc2d2aw38 mutants. Moreover, the antibody recognizes the truncated Cc2d2a protein generated by the W628X mutation when overexpressed in HEK293T cells (Fig. 3J). This band is absent in lysates from cc2d2a mutants, thereby indicating that no truncated Cc2d2a protein is present and that the cc2d2aw38 mutant used in this study is a protein null. Immunostaining on retinal cryosections at 4 and 5 d.p.f. confirms Cc2d2a localization at the base of acetylated tubulin- and Ift88-stained photoreceptor cilia (Fig. 3A–B′), just apical to gamma-tubulin staining (Fig. 3C and C′). Moreover, higher resolution images confirm Cc2d2a localization at the connecting cilium of zebrafish photoreceptors, since the Cc2d2a signal is (i) slightly apical to the basal-most acetylated tubulin staining (arrowhead in Fig. 3A″), (ii) just apical to gamma-tubulin staining of the basal body (Fig. 3C′) and (iii) contained in the Ift88-poor region previously shown to define the connecting cilium in photoreceptors (arrow in Fig. 3B′–B′″) (59). We used whole-mount embryos to assess cilia in other tissues and found that Cc2d2a is localized at the base of a variety of Arl13b-stained cilia, including motile cilia in 48 h.p.f. pronephric ducts (Fig. 3D and D′) and 24h.p.f. floorplate cells (Fig. 3E and E′), sensory cilia of 3 d.p.f. olfactory neurons (Fig. 3F) and primary cilia of 24 h.p.f. neuronal progenitors in the cerebellum (Fig. 3G and inset). This staining is entirely absent in cc2d2a−/− embryos (Supplementary Material, Fig. S2A–F), confirming the specificity of the antibody. Cc2d2a also localizes to the transition zone in neuronal progenitor cilia, where the Cc2d2a signal is detected between the gamma-tubulin basal body signal and the Arl13b axonemal signal (Fig. 3H), partially overlapping with each, as confirmed by fluorescence intensity graphs (Supplementary Material, Fig. S2G). Our previous description that CC2D2A and CEP290 co-localize in cultured cells further supports this finding, since CEP290 has also been shown to localize to the transition zone (39). Together, these data confirm localization of Cc2d2a to the connecting cilium in photoreceptors and to the transition zone of primary and motile cilia in a variety of cell types.

The products of other Joubert syndrome genes such as CEP290, AHI1, ARL13b or RPGRIP1L are thought to control ciliogenesis based on the observations that (i) cultured cells treated with siRNA/shRNA against CEP290 (43) or AHI1 (42) fail to extend cilia; (ii) mouse embryonic fibroblasts deficient for AHI1 have reduced numbers of cilia (42); and (iii) cilia are abnormal in zebrafish and mice deficient for Arl13b (11,60) and Rpgrip1l (61). In addition, Tallila et al. (49) reported that human fibroblasts with a truncating mutation in CC2D2A also lack cilia, supporting a role for CC2D2A in cilia formation. Since photoreceptor outer segments are highly specialized primary cilia, a defect in ciliogenesis could explain the outer segment phenotype observed in cc2d2a−/− fish. To test this hypothesis, we sought to determine whether cilia form normally in cc2d2a−/− retinas. Despite defective outer segment development in mutant photoreceptors, we observe structurally normal connecting cilia positioned apically within the inner segment using transmission electron microscopy (brackets in Fig. 4A and B, arrow in Fig. 6C and D). Furthermore, the total number of cilia is not decreased in mutant retinas as shown by acetylated tubulin immunostaining on whole-mount eyes from 5 d.p.f. Tg (TaCP: MCFP) cc2d2a−/− larvae (apical views in Fig. 4C–F): cc2d2a−/− eyes contain on average 13.1 ± 2.05 cilia/100 µm2 (n = 10 eyes) compared with 13.5 ± 1.6 cilia/100 µm2 in cc2d2a+/+ eyes (n = 5 eyes), P = 0.74 (Student's t-test). However, despite the normal density of cilia in mutant retinas, cilia length appeared decreased in mutants at the periphery of these whole-mount eyes, where the cilia can be viewed tangentially (Fig. 4E and F). To quantify the difference between wild-type and mutant axonemes, we measured the length of acetylated tubulin staining in equivalent retinal sections from multiple wild-type and mutant embryos at 7 d.p.f. (brackets in Fig. 4G and H). The average length of acetylated tubulin staining was 1.93 ± 0.87 µm in cc2d2a−/− photoreceptors compared with 3.8 ± 0.93 µm in cc2d2a+/+ or +/− photoreceptors (P < 0.0001, Student's t-test, n = 180 photoreceptors from 16 eyes). Although the length of the axoneme varies between different photoreceptor types (i.e. between cones and rods) and although some axonemes may leave the plane of the section, the results were very consistent across embryos and closely matched our observations in whole mounts. This does not reflect a general role for Cc2d2a in ciliogenesis or cilium extension, since many cell types that normally express Cc2d2a have normal-appearing cilia despite loss of Cc2d2a expression in cc2d2a mutants. Indeed, a variety of different cilia types are normal in cc2d2a−/− fish, including primary cilia in 24 h.p.f. retinal and neuronal progenitors (Fig. 4I–L, arrowheads in insets), as well as motile cilia in 24 h.p.f. floorplate (Fig. 4M and N) and 48 h.p.f. pronephric ducts (Fig. 4O and P). Similarly, olfactory cilia are indistinguishable between cc2d2a−/− and wild-type embryos at 3 d.p.f. (Fig. 4Q and R). For these experiments at early developmental stages (24 and 48 h.p.f.), we used embryos lacking both maternal and zygotic (mz) Cc2d2a to exclude the possibility that a mild phenotype at these earlier stages results from the perdurance of maternal gene product. While we cannot completely rule out a distinct role for Cc2d2a in photoreceptor axoneme elongation compared with other cell types, this possibility is unlikely based on the similar localization of Cc2d2a at the base of photoreceptors and other cilia, the presence of normal connecting cilia and normal-appearing axonemes in some mutant photoreceptors.

Proteins localized at the base of cilia can play a role in ciliogenesis but can also be involved in the transport of specific proteins to the ciliary membrane. This aspect of ciliary function has been particularly well studied in photoreceptors, since their outer segments are highly specialized primary cilia requiring massive transport of specific components (predominantly photopigments called opsins) (19). Opsins are transmembrane proteins that are normally targeted specifically to the outer segment by directed vesicle trafficking from the Golgi to the periciliary ridge complex, where fusion with the membrane occurs followed by IFT-dependent transport (20,62–64). Mutants in ciliopathy genes Cep290 and Ahi1 (45–47), as well as IFT components ift88, ift57 and Ift20 (8,65), exhibit mislocalization of opsins within the photoreceptor cell, suggesting a role for these proteins at one or more steps in the opsin transport.

We found a similar opsin mislocalization phenotype affecting both rod and cone photoreceptors in cc2d2a−/− fish. Immunostaining of 5 d.p.f. retinal cryosections with 4D2 (rhodopsin) and BOPS (blue cone opsin) antibodies showed that both rod and cone opsins are partially mislocalized throughout the photoreceptor cell (Fig. 5A–D). This is true not only in photoreceptors entirely lacking outer segments, but also in photoreceptors with grossly normal appearing, but shortened, outer segments. This trafficking defect does not affect all outer segment proteins, since transducin (66), a membrane-associated protein reaching the outer segment by diffusion (67,68), is not mislocalized in cc2d2a−/− photoreceptors (Fig. 5E and F). Moreover, trafficking towards other subcellular compartments occurs normally as well, as demonstrated by normal ribeye (69) localization to the synapse in cc2d2a−/− photoreceptors (Fig. 5G and H). Additional information about the role of Cc2d2a in opsin trafficking can be gained by determining the subcellular localization of ectopic opsins. For example, a recent study of a conditional mouse Ift20 mutant found that mislocalized opsins are concentrated in the Golgi, and thereby suggested a role for Ift20 in coupling the transport of opsins through the endomembrane system to the IFT system for transport into the cilium (65). We expressed a fusion protein in cc2d2a−/− embryos that specifically localizes to the Golgi of cone photoreceptors (gnat2:Man2a-RFP) (70) and observed little co-localization with the mislocalized cone opsin (Fig. 5I–I″), indicating that Cc2d2a functions downstream of the Golgi apparatus in the pathway transporting opsins to the outer segment. This is consistent with Cc2d2a localization only at the base of cilia and not at the Golgi apparatus. In addition to the accumulation of opsins in the apical portion of the mutant photoreceptors (inner segment area), we also observe mislocalization of opsins all along the cell membrane and in the basal portion of the photoreceptors near the synapse (arrow in Fig. 5J). To determine whether the mislocalized opsins are contained within the cell membrane or whether they accumulate in the cytoplasm, we performed co-staining with rhodopsin antibody (red) and phalloidin (green) to mark subcortical actin. In the majority of cases, the mislocalized rhodopsin (arrow) is present between the DAPI-stained nuclei and the phalloidin-stained actin network (arrowhead), thereby indicating that the majority of the mislocalized opsins are not inserted in the plasma membrane but accumulate in the cytoplasm (Fig. 5J). Together, these data indicate that Cc2d2a functions in a post-Golgi step for opsin-carrier vesicle trafficking to the cilium.

To further evaluate a possible role for Cc2d2a in vesicle fusion, we examined 5 d.p.f. retinas using transmission electron microscopy and identified striking accumulations of vesicles in cc2d2a−/− eyes (Fig. 6B and B′, C–F). These vesicles are particularly abundant in the apical-most portion of the photoreceptors (the inner segment), with accumulations around the connecting cilium and apical to the mitochondria (Fig. 6B and B′). In some photoreceptors, these vesicles entirely replace the membrane stacks of the outer segment (Fig. 6B, black and white bracket), but in most photoreceptors, they accumulate below short, partially disorganized stacks of membranes (Fig. 6C and E, black brackets). In addition, vesicles are also located more basally, lateral to the nucleus (Fig. 6E, red bracket; 6F, black bracket). Electron microscopy studies performed on zebrafish mutants lacking outer segments such as IFT mutants ift88 and ift172 have not found similar accumulation of vesicles despite complete lack of outer segments (9), indicating that accumulation of vesicles is not simply a consequence of deficient outer segment formation. The initial steps in vesicle trafficking, namely budding from the Golgi apparatus, appear unaffected in the cc2d2a mutant, since we did not observe significant ultra-structural anomalies of the Golgi in cc2d2a−/− photoreceptors by transmission electron microscopy (Fig. 6H). In addition, we mosaically expressed the Golgi marker gnat2:Man2a-RFP (70) in cone photoreceptors, using the transducin promoter, and observed no difference in Golgi morphology between wild-type and cc2d2a−/− fish (Fig. 6I and J). These data provide ultra-structural evidence supporting a role for Cc2d2a in vesicle fusion at the base of the photoreceptor cilium, but not in the earlier steps of vesicle budding from the Golgi. The small GTPase Rab8 is a key regulator of opsin-carrier vesicle trafficking in photoreceptors, based on the observation that a dominant-negative form of Rab8 leads to vesicle accumulation in Xenopus photoreceptors (21), similar to what we observe in cc2d2a mutants. This led us to evaluate whether Rab8 was normally localized in cc2d2a mutant photoreceptors. Since specific antibodies against zebrafish Rab8 are not available, we mosaically expressed a cherry-tagged Rab8 protein in cone photoreceptors using the transducin promoter. In cc2d2a+/+ and +/− photoreceptors, Rab8-cherry is concentrated in a single punctum at the base of the outer segment in 66% of expressing cells (Fig. 7A and A′ and Supplementary Material, Fig. S3E, quantification in Fig. 7C), consistent with a previous description for Rab8 localization in Xenopus photoreceptors using a Rab8-GFP construct (21). In the cc2d2a−/− siblings, this punctate localization is observed in only 26% of expressing cells, whereas most cells show diffuse expression throughout the cytoplasm with occasional weak concentration in the inner segment (brackets in Fig. 7B and B′, quantification in Fig. 7C), indicating that Cc2d2a is at least partially required for punctate localization of Rab8 in the inner segment. To test whether Cc2d2a localization is dependent on Rab8, we used a previously described splice-blocking rab8 morpholino (71) which causes a sinusoidal body shape and a retinal phenotype (shortened outer segments and rhodopsin mislocalization) similar to cc2d2a mutants (Supplementary Material, Fig. S3A–D). Despite this retinal phenotype in Rab8 morphants, Cc2d2a localization at the base of photoreceptor cilia is unaffected (Fig. 7D). Together, these data indicate that Rab8 localization depends on Cc2d2a, whereas Cc2d2a localization occurs independently of Rab8.
